To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fully connected layers are inefficient for smaller batches, accuracy and inference time is a hyperbolic relation, energy is an upper bound on accuracy and model complexity, and the number of operations are a good predictor of the inference time.

(1) the number of layers, operations count and inference time are hyperbolically correlated; (2) energy constraints are an upper bound for the maximum achievable accuracy; (3) fully connected layers can be replaced by a convolutional layer for small batch size images.
